content.title: Where to Watch the Mavs | Dallas Mavericks
content.text: Frequently Asked QuestionsOur goal is to make it as easy for as many Mavs fans to watch Mavs games as possible. Partnering with WFAA Ch.8 and KFAA Ch. 29 allows us to reach over 3.1 million households for free, over-the-air. This is just one of many investments the Mavs plan to make to further engage and respond to our growing fan base.MFFLs living in the DFW metroplex and surrounding areas will be able to watch the Mavs on WFAA Ch. 8 (15 games) and KFAA Ch. 29 (ALL non-exclusive national games) for FREE over-the-air with the use of a digital tv antenna. For more on how free over-the-air tv works, or to learn how to set up an antenna, visit wfaa.com/kfaa.KFAA is a full power UHF (ultra high frequency), high-definition station owned and operated by WFAA parent company TEGNA. As a UHF station KFAA’s signal strength is stronger than WFAA.Newly rebranded TEGNA station KFAA Dallas-Ft. Worth (Ch. 29), which launched new programming on October 20, 2024, will broadcast all games not exclusively televised nationally – for free over-the-air. Games airing on KFAA in the Dallas-Ft. Worth market will be available through the following providers: AT&T U-verse TV, Charter Spectrum, DIRECTV, DIRECTV Stream, DISH, Frontier Fiber Keller, Fubo, GEUS, Grande Communications, OneSource Communications and Optimum. A minimum of 15 games in the 2025-26 season will air on WFAA Ch. 8, and all non national exclusive regular season games (including the 15 on WFAA) will air on KFAA Ch. 29. Fifteen-time Emmy Award-winning play-by-play announcer Mark Followill, now entering his 21st season, will again serve as the voice of the Mavs television broadcast. Followill will be joined by analysts Devin Harris, entering his third season, Derek Harper, entering his 15th season, and Jeff “Skin” Wade, entering his 18th season. Lesley McCaslin will serve as the Mavericks’ sideline reporter for the third consecutive season, and Dana Larson will helm Mavs CenterCourt as she enters her 18th season serving as the team’s pre- and postgame host. Harris, Harper, and Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Famer Nancy Lieberman will join Larson at the desk throughout the season, alongside a lineup of special guests, including Mavs legends Tyson Chandler, Josh Howard and Avery Johnson. All non-national games will also be broadcast on TEGNA stations in Waco (KCEN), Bryan/College Station (KAGS), Tyler-Longview (KYTX), Midland-Odessa (KWES), Abilene (KXVA), El Paso (KDBC), Amarillo (KFDA), Lubbock (KCBD, and KLCW), Wichita Falls & Lawton, OK (KJBO), Sherman (KXII), Texarkana & Shreveport, LA (KSHV), Laredo (KXNU, KGNS, and KYLX), Harlingen-Weslaco-Brownsville-McAllen (KGBT), and San Angelo (KIDY). The station websites and local game listings from your distributor will be updated as the season progresses. You must be within the available local broadcast territory to stream Mavs games on MavsTV. Check your zip code above to see if you are eligible for MavsTV. Out of market Mavs fans can watch games via NBA League Pass – the league’s live game out of market subscription service at https://www.nba.com/watch/league-pass-stream.
